Subject: Internal: PHI retention/redaction options (draft)

Folks — draft matrix below. I'll turn into a one-pager for Rachel to send out. Notes include practical implementation patterns (what we can enforce in-hosting vs what requires customer-side ETL).

Option A — Minimal (developer-friendly)
- Hot cache: KV cache TTL 2 hours (purpose: latency)
- Cold store (model input logs): 30 days
- Embeddings/vector store TTL: 60 days (evict and re-embed on demand)
- Backups: encrypted snapshots retained 90 days; on-delete we mark and sweep next snapshot window
- Redaction: read-time masking + field-level tokenization for high-risk fields
- Tradeoffs: easiest for debugging, higher residual risk and longer artifact lifetime

Option B — Moderate (balanced)
- Hot cache: KV cache TTL 30 minutes; purge on tenant soft-delete
- Cold store: 14 days retention for raw inputs; logs persisted with pseudonymized IDs for 365 days for audit (PII fields removed)
- Embeddings: store hashed/non-reversible embeddings for 90 days; provide policy to reindex if needed
- Backups: 45-day retention for incremental backups; retention reduced if data tagged PHI
- Redaction: field-level irreversible hashing for identifiers + reversible tokenization for debugging (keys rotated and access audited)
- Tradeoffs: reasonable debugging, reduced exposure, increased operational complexity

Option C — Strict (regulated workload)
- Hot cache: zero persistent KV caching for sensitive fields; ephemeral only during inference
- Cold store: 0–7 day retention for raw PHI depending on contract; all long-tail data redacted at write-time
- Embeddings: do not store embeddings derived from direct identifiers; if stored, irreversible and non-linkable
- Backups: exclude PHI fields from long-term snapshots; deletion requires explicit verification and snapshot reconstitution to purge
- Redaction: write-time field scrubbing + irreversible transformation; read-time rehydration only via customer-side tokens
- Tradeoffs: highest compliance, hardest for support and model troubleshooting

Operational notes:
- Deletion proofs: we can provide a signed timestamped audit entry per tenant deletion + manifest of deleted object IDs; full cryptographic proof (hash chains) is available on request but increases cost and latency.
- Legal hold: retains items regardless of retention policy; we flag and exclude from automatic sweep. Requires a signed request and SCIM integration for lifecycle state.

Attachments recommended to send: redwood_redaction_playbook_v1.pdf, retention-slas-and-proofs.xlsx, SOC2_excerpt.pdf

-Neha

Couple of caveats to call out for the one-pager:
- Redaction-at-write is the strongest signal for regulators, but it means we can[0m't reproduce exact inputs for model quality checks. Recommend a hybrid: irreversible hash of patient identifiers + reversible debugging token available only to a limited ops role (audited).
- Embeddings: even irreversible embeddings can leak; for strict profiles we recommend not storing embeddings beyond session. If persist, store per-customer namespace with per-customer encryption keys (KMS/HSM) and short TTLs.
- Cache eviction: we support tenant-scoped eviction API. For guaranteed removal, trigger eviction + async background sweep that scrubs intermediate caches and index shards. We should document the sweep SLA (e.g., full tenant sweep within 24 hours of request).
- Proofs: signed manifest + snapshot id is pragmatic. If they want verifiable hash chains for each deleted object, that[0m's available but will be an add-on.

I'll add a short "what you lose" section (debugging capabilities that change per option) and propose suggested default = Option B for the pilot.

-Karthik

Sarah — attached is a one-page summary and the short playbook excerpt Neha mentioned (see attachments). TL;DR recommendation for pilot: Option B (Moderate) with the following specifics we can operationalize quickly:
- Raw inputs retained 14 days (US region only)
- Embeddings retained 90 days as irreversible hashes; option to re-embed on demand
- KV cache TTL 30 minutes for tenant-scoped keys; full tenant sweep SLA = 24 hours after deletion request
- Backups: incremental 45-day retention; PHI excluded from long-term snapshots when flagged
- Deletion proof: signed manifest + snapshot id provided within 48 hours of completion
- Legal hold: supported via SCIM lifecycle flag; items under hold excluded from sweeps

Tradeoffs and asks for Clarify Health:
- If you need write-time irreversible redaction for all PHI, that will limit our ability to replay inputs for model diagnostics; suggest allowing reversible debug tokens for a small ops group during pilot.
- Confirm procurement SLA window and whether the signed deletion manifest is sufficient or if you require hash-chain proofs.

Next steps: please confirm preferred option and procurement timeline; we can schedule a short call with engineering to walk the deletion sweep flow and show the tenant-sweep demo.

Best,
